message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "15 0 * * *"
    - cron: "15 23 * * *"
  push:
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
      - ".examples/**"
      - ".githooks/**"
      - "charts/**"
      - "docker/**"
    branches:
      - main
      - v5.x
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
      - ".examples/**"
      - ".githooks/**"
      - "charts/**"
      - "docker/**"
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  MAVEN_ARGS: "--no-transfer-progress --errors --fail-at-end --show-version"
  PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD: 1  # required browsers are installed below

jobs:
  build:
    name: build and analyse
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up JDK from .tool-versions
        uses: actions/setup-java@77dd5b2ce225ea11469928ac317850245a74ae78
        with:
          java-version-file: ".tool-versions"
          cache: 'maven'

      - name: Build
        run: ./mvnw -Pcoverage dependency:go-offline clean verify -Dgroups="!ui"

      - name: Analyse with SonarCloud
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]') }}
        run: >
          ./mvnw
          -Pcoverage
          sonar:sonar
          -Dsonar.host.url=https://sonarcloud.io
          -Dsonar.organization=urlaubsverwaltung
          -Dsonar.projectKey=urlaubsverwaltung_urlaubsverwaltung
          -Dsonar.coverage.jacoco.xmlReportPaths=target/site/jacoco/jacoco.xml,target/site/jacoco-it/jacoco.xml
          -Dsonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths=target/js-coverage/lcov.info
          -Dsonar.javascript.exclusions=**/__tests__/**,**/*-spec.js,**/*.spec.js,**/*-test.js,**/*.test.js
          -Dsonar.eslint.reportPaths=target/js-eslint/report.json
          -Dsonar.coverage.exclusions=**/__tests__/**,**/*-spec.js,**/*.spec.js,**/*-test.js,**/*.test.js
          -Dsonar.sources=src/main
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}

  ui-test:
    name: UI Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        browser: ["chromium", "firefox", "webkit"]
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-ui-test-${{ matrix.browser }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up JDK from .tool-versions
        uses: actions/setup-java@77dd5b2ce225ea11469928ac317850245a74ae78
        with:
          java-version-file: ".tool-versions"
          cache: 'maven'

      - name: Cache Playwright browsers
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        id: playwright-cache
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ matrix.browser }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pom.xml') }}

      - name: Install Playwright Browsers (UI tests)
        if: steps.playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: ./mvnw exec:java -e -D exec.mainClass=com.microsoft.playwright.CLI -D exec.classpathScope="test" -D exec.args="install ${{matrix.browser}}"

      - name: Install Playwright System Deps (UI tests)
        run: ./mvnw exec:java -e -D exec.mainClass=com.microsoft.playwright.CLI -D exec.classpathScope="test" -D exec.args="install-deps ${{matrix.browser}}"

      - name: Test
        run: ./mvnw dependency:go-offline verify -Pui-test -Dbrowser=${{matrix.browser}}

      - name: Upload artifacts of failed tests
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
        if: ${{ always() && hashFiles(format('target/ui-test/{0}/FAILED-*', matrix.browser)) != '' }}
        with:
          name: urlaubsverwaltung-failed-ui-tests-${{ matrix.browser }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: target/ui-test/${{matrix.browser}}/FAILED-*

  a11y-test:
    name: Accessibility Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        browser: ["chromium", "firefox", "webkit"]
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-a11y-test-${{ matrix.browser }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up JDK from .tool-versions
        uses: actions/setup-java@77dd5b2ce225ea11469928ac317850245a74ae78
        with:
          java-version-file: ".tool-versions"
          cache: 'maven'

      - name: Install Playwright Browsers (A11Y tests)
        run: ./mvnw exec:java -e -D exec.mainClass=com.microsoft.playwright.CLI -D exec.classpathScope="test" -D exec.args="install --with-deps ${{matrix.browser}}"

      - name: Test
        run: ./mvnw dependency:go-offline verify -Pa11y-test -Dbrowser=${{matrix.browser}}

      - name: Upload artifacts of failed tests
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
        if: ${{ always() && hashFiles('target/a11y-test/**/FAILED-*') != '' }}
        with:
          name: failed-a11y-tests-${{ matrix.browser }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: target/a11y-test/**/FAILED-*

  visual-test:
    name: Visual Regression Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-visual-test
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      # without git-lfs, a changed baseline is committed as regular git object and grows the repository permanently
      - name: Check that baselines are committed as LFS pointers
        run: git lfs fsck --pointers

      # baselines are stored in git lfs, cached to not use up the lfs bandwidth with every build
      - name: List LFS objects
        run: git lfs ls-files --long | cut -d ' ' -f1 | sort > .lfs-objects

      - name: Cache LFS objects
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .git/lfs
          key: lfs-${{ hashFiles('.lfs-objects') }}
          restore-keys: lfs-

      - name: Pull LFS objects
        run: git lfs pull

      - name: Set up JDK from .tool-versions
        uses: actions/setup-java@77dd5b2ce225ea11469928ac317850245a74ae78
        with:
          distribution: 'liberica'
          java-version-file: ".tool-versions"
          cache: 'maven'

      # starts the application with an empty database and the browser server in the pinned container, see
      # docs/visual-regression-tests.md. no browser matrix, the screenshots are rendered by chromium only.
      - name: Test
        run: ./mvnw dependency:go-offline verify -Pvisual-test

      - name: Upload artifacts of failed tests
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        with:
          name: failed-visual-tests-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            target/visual-tests/report
            target/visual-tests/results",
  "rationale": "Add a custom timeout to the build job based on P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT evidence. The experiment (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) showed a 26.8% elapsed time reduction by adding a 5-minute timeout to a job with ~34s median runtime. The build job currently lacks a timeout while all other jobs (ui-test, a11y-test, visual-test) have 20-minute timeouts. Historical runs show ~12-minute total workflow duration; a 20-minute timeout provides operational headroom over the build job's expected runtime while preventing runaway consumption. This change preserves all build and test coverage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}

The user wants me to analyze the provided workflow and evidence to propose a CI optimization. Let me first understand the workflow and the evidence.

The workflow is a Maven-based Java project with multiple jobs:
1. `build` - builds and analyzes with SonarCloud
2. `ui-test` - UI tests with Playwright across 3 browsers (matrix)
3. `a11y-test` - Accessibility tests across 3 browsers (matrix)
4. `visual-test` - Visual regression tests (single job)

The evidence includes several experiment examples and pattern catalog entries. Let me look at the relevant ones:

1. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - Experiment shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job reduced elapsed time by ~27%. The workflow already has timeouts on some jobs (ui-test, a11y-test, visual-test have 20 minutes), but the `build` job doesn't have a timeout.

2. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** - Experiments show setting `fail-fast: true` on matrix jobs. The workflow currently has `fail-fast: false` on both ui-test and a11y-test matrix jobs.

3. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - The workflow already has `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` on all jobs.

4. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - The workflow uses Maven cache via `setup-java` with `cache: 'maven'` and also caches Playwright browsers and LFS objects.

5. **P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER** - The workflow already has `paths-ignore` on push and pull_request triggers.

Now, looking at the workflow:
- The `build` job has no timeout (could add one based on P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
- The `ui-test` and `a11y-test` matrix jobs have `fail-fast: false` (could change to `true` based on P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)
- The `visual-test` job has no matrix, so fail-fast doesn't apply

Let me check the evidence more carefully:

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: The experiment shows a 26.8% elapsed savings by adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job that had median runtime of 34 seconds. The `build` job in this workflow likely takes longer (Maven build with tests). But the pattern says "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom" and "Measure false timeout failures separately". The reported result shows 12.9% free / 8.1% paid VM time reduction.

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: The experiments show changing `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true` on matrix jobs. The workflow has two matrix jobs (ui-test and a11y-test) both with `fail-fast: false`. The pattern says "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy". The reported result shows 2% free / 1.5% paid VM time reduction.

Both seem applicable. However, I need to check preconditions and contraindications.

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST:
- Preconditions: "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy"
- Contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required", "Full failure diagnostics are required"

For UI tests and accessibility tests across browsers, if one browser fails, do we need the others to continue? Typically for cross-browser testing, you might want to see all browser results. But the pattern suggests if failure in one makes others dispensable, you can enable fail-fast.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT:
- Preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists"
- Contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit"

The build job doesn't have a timeout currently. Looking at the CI history, the runs take about 12-13 minutes (from created_at to updated_at). So a timeout of maybe 20-30 minutes could be reasonable.

But wait - the experiment example for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows a Node.js workflow, not Maven. The pattern is general though.

Now, the instruction says: "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization that fits this workflow; there is no fixed optimization-type allowlist. Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes."

I need to choose ONE optimization (or possibly multiple if they're compatible) and provide the updated workflow.

Looking at the evidence IDs provided in the prompt:
- experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242 (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997 (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)
- experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-430562ddbb0b29c9-r2 (P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP)

The P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP is about skipping unused dependency updates, which doesn't seem directly applicable to this Maven workflow (it's more about npm).

Between P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, both have experimental evidence. The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has two experiment examples showing the same change (fail-fast: false -> true). The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has one experiment example.

The workflow has two matrix jobs with fail-fast: false. Changing them to true would be a minimal change.

However, I need to consider: for UI tests and accessibility tests, if one browser fails, is it useful to continue running the others? In many cases, yes - you want to know which browsers pass/fail. But the pattern says "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy". This is a policy decision.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT could be applied to the `build` job which currently has no timeout. The median runtime from history is ~12 minutes. A timeout of 20 minutes (with headroom) could prevent runaway builds.

Let me check the workflow again for existing timeouts:
- build: no timeout
- ui-test: timeout-minutes: 20
- a11y-test: timeout-minutes: 20
- visual-test: timeout-minutes: 20

So only the build job lacks a timeout. Adding one there would be consistent.

The experiment for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT added `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job that ran in ~34 seconds median. That's a very tight timeout (5 min vs 34 sec). For a 12-minute build, a 20-minute timeout would be similar ratio (20 min vs 12 min = 1.67x vs 5 min vs 0.57 min = 8.8x). Actually 34 seconds is 0.57 minutes, so 5 minutes is ~8.8x. For 12 minutes, 8.8x would be ~105 minutes. But the pattern says "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom". A 20-minute timeout (1.67x) might be too tight for cold runs.

Looking at the CI history: the successful runs take about 12 minutes (from created_at to updated_at). But that's the whole workflow, not just the build job. The build job is likely the longest.

Actually, looking at the timestamps:
- Run 43818055831: created 06:37:44, updated 06:50:39 = ~13 minutes
- Run 43794138500: created 02:46:06, updated 02:58:09 = ~12 minutes
- Run 43591934893: created 11:50:40, updated 12:02:39 = ~12 minutes

These are scheduled runs. The build job probably takes 8-10 minutes.

Given the evidence, I think both optimizations are supported. But I need to pick one (or both if they don't conflict). The instruction says "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization" - singular "optimization" but could be multiple changes.

However, the output format expects a single decision and a single workflow_yaml. I can include multiple changes in the workflow_yaml.

Let me think about which has stronger evidence:
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Two experiment examples showing the exact same change (fail-fast: false -> true) on matrix jobs. Outcome: "scenario_passed". But limitations: "Synthetic workload: timings are scenario resource costs, not original repository CI savings."
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: One experiment example on a Node.js workflow, measured on fork, 26.8% elapsed savings. Outcome: null. But it's a measured CI workflow on fork.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT experiment is more realistic (measured_ci_workflow_on_fork vs synthetic_fixture_on_dedicated_fork).

Also, the workflow already has timeouts on the matrix jobs (20 minutes), but not on the build job. Adding a timeout to the build job would be a new protection.

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, the workflow has `fail-fast: false` explicitly set. Changing to `true` would be a behavior change.

I think P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is safer and more universally applicable. The build job has no timeout, and adding one prevents runaway builds. The experiment shows significant savings.

But wait - the experiment added timeout-minutes: 5 to a job that had no timeout. The workflow's build job has no timeout. So it's directly analogous.

Let me check the pattern catalog for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: "Custom timeouts reduce runaway consumption." VM time reduction: free 12.9%, paid 8.1%.

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: "Matrix cancellation saves remaining work." VM time reduction: free 2%, paid 1.5%.

The custom timeout has higher reported savings.

Also, the build job is run on every trigger (schedule, push, PR, workflow_dispatch), while the matrix jobs only run on certain triggers? Actually all jobs run on all triggers based on the workflow.

But the build job is a single job, while ui-test and a11y-test are 3 jobs each (matrix of 3 browsers). So there are more matrix job runs.

However, the custom timeout applies to every run of the build job, while fail-fast only saves time when there's a failure.

Given the evidence, I'll propose adding a custom timeout to the build job. I'll set it to 20 minutes (similar to the other jobs) which gives ~2x headroom over the observed ~12 minute total workflow time (build job likely 8-10 min).

Actually, looking at the other jobs, they have 20-minute timeouts. The build job is likely the longest. Let me set it to 30 minutes to be safe.

But the experiment used 5 minutes for a 34-second job. That's huge headroom. For a 10-minute job, 30 minutes is 3x headroom.

I'll go with 20 minutes to match the other jobs.

Now, I need to produce the updated workflow YAML with the change.

The change: add `timeout-minutes: 20` to the `build` job.

Let me write the updated workflow.

Also, I need to include the evidence IDs. For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, the experiment ID is `experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508`. The pattern catalog also has `pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT`.

The instruction says: "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one."

I'll use the experiment ID.

Now, the decision: APPLY with the updated workflow.

Rationale: Add custom timeout to build job based on P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT evidence showing 26.8% elapsed savings in measured CI workflow experiment. The build job currently lacks a timeout while other jobs have 20-minute timeouts. Adding a 20-minute timeout prevents runaway consumption with operational headroom over observed ~12-minute workflow duration.

Evidence IDs: ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]

Let me construct the full workflow YAML.
